prediction:
MECHANISM.  #13's geom.c half landed the derived edge-priority order -- for a
triangle (a, b, c) paint the edge opposite a, then opposite b, then opposite c
-- and took nine of eleven candidate classes to 100.00% of their decisive
pixels.  TFan stopped at the PRE-REGISTERED 70.36% and QStrip/TFan at 77.17%,
because rewrite_triangle_fan() calls emit_tri_pv(), which rotates the guest's
provoking vertex to index 0: a fan triangle reaches geom.c already rotated by
one relative to the TRIANGLES draw beside it, and GeomState::primitive_mode is
the REWRITTEN mode, so geom.c cannot tell them apart and cannot compensate.

THIS ARM removes that rotation in exactly the state where nothing reads index
0.  Both renderers rasterise first-vertex-provoking (gl/draw.c sets
GL_FIRST_VERTEX_CONVENTION; nothing in vk/ enables VK_EXT_provoking_vertex)
and geom.c spells provoking_index as the literal "0" only when the shade mode
is FLAT -- needs_rewrite() already encodes that for PRIM_TYPE_TRIANGLES, which
it declines to rewrite at all unless the draw is flat AND last-provoking.  The
new predicate is `flat_shading || polygon_mode != POLY_MODE_LINE`, so the fan
keeps its rotation under FILL, under POINT, and under flat shading everywhere.
#13's trade is NARROWED to its one real corner -- a flat-shaded wireframe,
where the colour must win over the paint order -- not abolished.

WHY IT IS FREE ON THE WIREFRAME PATH.  geom.c splits a triangle (A, B, C) into
emit_line(B,C), emit_line(C,A), emit_line(A,B).  Rotating the triple is
therefore a pure rotation of the EDGE LIST: the multiset of ORDERED (i0, i1)
pairs is identical and only the paint order changes.  That is checked, not
argued -- see the A/B below, where the old code emits 2 0 1 / 3 0 2 / ... and
the new emits 0 1 2 / 0 2 3 / ..., the same ordered pairs in a rotated order.
So vtxFogSpecial, which glsl/common.c qualifies `flat` in EVERY shade mode but
which each emit_line() takes from that edge's OWN first endpoint rather than
from the triangle's index 0, is unchanged per edge.

THE SCOPE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED.  Both revisions of prim_rewrite.c were
compiled side by side and their output diffed over every
(primitive_mode x polygon_mode x last_provoking x flat_shading x count)
combination, 1508 states: exactly 20 differ, all of them TRIANGLE_FAN under
POLY_MODE_LINE with smooth shading, at both provoking conventions, with an
IDENTICAL index count on every one.  A reorder emits the same number of lines,
so no counter can tell the two arms apart and only the captures can.

THE OFFLINE MODEL IS CALIBRATED ON THE LANDED ARM, TO THE PIXEL.  Running
`docs/testing/line_priority.py --rules --max-width 63.875` against the
Line_width goldens reproduces the geom.c arm's measured arm-B table on ALL
ELEVEN classes and the aggregate, with every n identical: Tri 45,760 100.00%,
QStrip 35,560 100.00%, LLoop 31,548 99.53%, QStrip/TFan 22,897 77.17%, Quad
22,761 100.00%, Poly 15,235 100.00%, Poly/TFan 13,853 100.00%, TFan 9,731
70.36%, LLoop/Tri 1,305 100.00%, Poly/Tri 222 100.00%, LLoop/TFan 8 100.00%,
ALL 198,880 95.85%.  Eleven ns and twelve percentages, none fitted.  That is
what makes the values below predictions rather than hopes -- and the tool
needed fixing first to get there: its hand-listed `ours` table predated BOTH
halves of #13's edge-order work and still described the pre-fold order for
Tri, QStrip, Poly and Quad, so the column scored a renderer we stopped being
two folds ago.  It is now derived from prim_rewrite.c composed with geom.c.

A CORRECTION TO THE NUMBER THIS WORK HAS BEEN CARRYING.  #13's comments, and
this lane's own brief, call the residue "32,628 decisive pixels".  That is the
POPULATION of the two classes (9,731 + 22,897), not the pixels that are wrong
inside it.  The pixels that actually name the wrong edge are 2,884 in TFan
(9,731 - 70.36%) and 5,228 in QStrip/TFan (22,897 - 77.17%): 8,112 in total,
which is also exactly the gap between the two rule columns (198,731 - 190,619).
Registering 32,628 as the expected movement would have been wrong by 4x.

LEG 1 -- TFan, 9,731 decisive pixels: 70.36% -> 100.00%.  The world in which
it fails: 70.36% unchanged (the patch did not reach the device, or the
predicate never fires); 47.57%, which is the pre-geom.c value and would mean
the composition is being undone rather than completed; or any other value,
which refutes the model that a fan triangle is pre-rotated by exactly one.

LEG 2 -- QStrip/TFan, 22,897 decisive pixels: 77.17% -> 100.00%.  This is the
harder half and it is a MIXED class: the pixel is decided by a fan edge's rank
against a QUAD_STRIP edge emitted by a different code path that this patch does
not touch.  It can fail while leg 1 passes, and it fails at 77.17%
(unchanged), at 100.00%-minus-anything, or if QStrip itself moves.

LEG 3, scope -- the nine other classes are UNCHANGED and `moved` is 0 on each
one: Tri 100.00%, QStrip 100.00%, LLoop 99.53%, Quad 100.00%, Poly 100.00%,
Poly/TFan 100.00%, LLoop/Tri 100.00%, Poly/Tri 100.00%, LLoop/TFan 100.00%.
Poly/TFan and LLoop/TFan are the ones that can fail: they CONTAIN fan edges
whose rank this patch changes, and the claim is that the winner does not
change even though the rank does.  A leg that only named the fan-free classes
would be forced true by the patch.

LEG 4, did it execute -- `moved` (decisive pixels where arm A and arm B name
DIFFERENT edges) is at least 2,884 on TFan and at least 5,228 on QStrip/TFan.
A patch that never reached the device gives moved = 0 on every class and is
otherwise indistinguishable, in any pixel total, from one that ran and
returned a different wrong answer.  Arm A against itself gives 0 by
construction, so this leg has a world in which it fails.

LEG 5, THE TRADE'S OWN GUARD -- every `Shade_model/*_TriFan_Flat_*` capture is
BYTE-IDENTICAL (14 captures: seven shader prefixes x First/Last).  Under flat
shading pv_placement_observable() returns true and rewrite_triangle_fan() is
untouched, so these must not move at all.  This is the leg that would catch
the predicate being inverted or the flat_shading term being dropped, and its
failure would be large rather than subtle: a flat-shaded fan whose provoking
vertex moved changes the colour of whole triangles, not a few edge pixels.

LEG 6, primitive scope on the same suite -- `Shade_model/*_Tri_*`,
`*_TriStrip_*`, `*_Quad_*`, `*_QuadStrip_*` and `*_Poly_*` are all
BYTE-IDENTICAL.  The patch reaches PRIM_TYPE_TRIANGLE_FAN and nothing else;
TRIANGLE_STRIP in particular is deliberately left alone, because its odd-i
case is a reflection rather than a rotation and the Line_width corpus that
pins these orders draws no TRIANGLE_STRIP under POLY_MODE_LINE at all.

LEG 7, advisory and NOT counted -- ALL rises from 95.85% to 99.93% over
198,880 decisive pixels, leaving 149 px, of which LLoop's known 99.53%
accounts for about 148.  Advisory because it is legs 1-3 re-added and the
pooled figure hides which class moved.

EXPECTED TO MOVE, direction unpredicted, named so a mover is not read as a
surprise: `Shade_model/*_TriFan_Smooth_*` (14 captures -- these are the ones
that CAN reach the patch), every per-capture differing-pixel total in
`Line width`, and any `Edge flag` / `Front face` / `W param` capture that
draws a TRIANGLE_FAN under POLY_MODE_LINE.  Direction is unpredicted for the
reason #13 recorded: the decisive set is ~0.1% of the ink and the priority
class overlaps the extent class, so removing a priority error need not reduce
any total.  ONE SECOND-ORDER ITEM, disclosed rather than buried: geom.c's
POLY_MODE_LINE body takes its depth slope from calc_triz(0, 1, 2), which
computes m and b relative to vertex 0, so a fan triangle's dz is now evaluated
on the same basis a list triangle's already was.  The plane's gradient is
rotation-invariant, so this can move dz only by rounding, and it feeds triMZ
(depth) and not coverage; `Line width` disables the depth test, so it cannot
show there at all.

THE DISC carries Blend_tests, which draws no wide line and no wireframe at
all, for the same reason lane.linecap13 put it there: it is the tripwire for
this change being broader than modelled.  Legs 5 and 6 cover 154 of
Shade_model's 168 captures -- everything but the 14 `*_TriFan_Smooth_*` that
can legitimately move.

NOT A FALSIFIER, recorded as an assertion about my own output: `2D_Lines/*`
byte-identical.  PRIMITIVE_LINES never reaches rewrite_triangle_fan(), so my
own patch forces it true and it tests nothing about silicon.
